text.p: Lithuania's Prosecutor General Vladas Nikitinas resigned on Monday amid continuing controversy over steps to clamp down on organised crime and corruption in the Baltic state.

Lithuania's new right-wing government, which ousted former communists in a parliamentary election last November, has launched a major drive to crack down on organised crime in the former Soviet republic.
This has included moves to reform the prosecutor's office. Interfax news agency on Monday reported accusations that the department had been infiltrated by criminal networks.
"I see no further point in continuing my work because of the complicated crime situation in the country," Nikitinas told Reuters by telephone after submitting his resignation to the president.
"Fresh forces are necessary who probably might undertake a new approach and find new ways to stabilise the situation of expanding crime."
Nikitinas, 55, who stepped into the office in December 1994, said he would return to working as a lawyer in the country's courts.
Nikitinas said he informed Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius about his decision at a meeting of law enforcement agencies on Saturday.
This group is helping the government draft a new bill to fight organised crime that is expected to go before parliament by February.
"Major attention will be given to reforming the prosecutor's office and police," a government statement said on Monday.
